1. A method of assembling a tool adapted for insertion into a physiological lumen of a patient:
obtaining a core, the core having an elongate shape;
disposing a printed circuit board (PCB) assembly onto the core, the PCB assembly including a PCB substrate and an electronic component disposed on the PCB substrate;
coupling the PCB substrate to the core;
electrically coupling the electronic component to a hub coupled to the core; and
applying an outer sheath about the core and the PCB assembly.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the PCB substrate includes an adhesive backing and coupling the PCB substrate to the core comprises bonding the PCB substrate to the core using the adhesive backing.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein applying the outer sheath about the core and the PCB assembly couples the PCB substrate to the core.
4. The method of claim 1 further comprising, after applying the outer sheath, removing a portion of the outer sheath to expose the electronic component.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the core is a tubular core and the tool is a catheter.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the PCB substrate is preformed into a ring shape.
7. The method of claim 1 further comprising forming the PCB substrate into a ring shape.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein applying the outer sheath about the core and the PCB assembly couples the PCB substrate to a distal end of the core.
9. The method of claim 1, wherein PCB substrate is flexible and coupling the PCB substrate to the core includes wrapping the PCB substrate about a portion of the core.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the PCB assembly includes a terminal point and a trace extending along the PCB substrate, and wherein electrically coupling the electronic component to the hub includes electrically coupling the terminal point to the hub.
11. The method of claim 1, wherein:
the PCB assembly includes a terminal point and a trace extending along the PCB substrate, electrically coupling the electronic component to the hub includes electrically coupling the terminal point to the hub, the PCB substrate extends distally from a proximal end of the core, the terminal point is disposed at the proximal end of the core, and
the electronic component is disposed distally from the terminal point.
12. The method of claim 1, wherein the electronic component is an electrode.
13. The method of claim 1, wherein the electronic component is an electrode disposed at a distal end of the core.
14. The method of claim 1, wherein the electronic component is an electrode and the electrode extends circumferentially about the tubular core.
15. The method of claim 1, wherein the PCB substrate is a multi-part ring.
16. The method of claim 1, wherein the core is a catheter shaft.
17. The method of claim 1, wherein the electronic component is a sensor.
18. A method of assembling a tool adapted for insertion into a physiological lumen of a patient:
obtaining a core, the core having an elongate shape;
disposing a printed circuit board (PCB) assembly onto the core, the PCB assembly including a PCB substrate, a first electrode disposed on the PCB substrate and electrically coupled to a first terminal point of the PCB assembly, and a second electrode disposed on the PCB substrate and electrically coupled to a second terminal point of the PCB assembly;
coupling the PCB substrate to the core;
electrically coupling each of the first electrode and the second electrode to the electronic component to a hub coupled to the core; and
applying an outer sheath about the core and the PCB assembly.
19. The method of claim 18, wherein, after applying the outer sheath, each of the first electrode and the second electrode are exposed through the outer sheath.
20. A method of assembling a tool adapted for insertion into a physiological lumen of a patient:
obtaining a core, the core having an elongate shape;
disposing a printed circuit board (PCB) assembly onto the core, the PCB assembly including a PCB substrate having a preformed ring shape and an electronic component disposed on the PCB substrate;
disposing the PCB substrate onto the core;
electrically coupling the electronic component to a hub coupled to the core; and
coupling the PCB substrate to a distal end of the core by applying an outer sheath about each of the core and the PCB assembly. 13459USD125PATENT 13459USD126PATENT 13459USD127PATENT
